en: The Mogao Caves are located within a close distance south-east of the oasis town of Dunhuang 敦煌, which was established as a frontier garrison outpost in the second century BCE and came to be a strategic spot at the cross of the Northern and the Southern Silk Roads. The first cave is said to have been carved in 366 CE by a Buddhist pilgrim monk and, over the next millennium, almost 1,000 caves and niches were gradually excavated in
zh: 莫高位于敦煌东南不远处，而敦煌则是一座始建于公元前二世纪的边防要塞，后来逐渐发展成为连接南北丝绸之路的战略要地。据传第一座洞窟是由一位佛教朝圣僧人在公元366年开凿的，此后的一千多年间，那里陆续挖掘出了近1000座洞窟和壁龛。

en: Perhaps hoping to get some form of financial compensation or recognition for his pious endeavours, Wang Yuanlu immediately went to report the discovery to the local county magistrate, Yan Ze 嚴澤(dates unknown). He took two manuscripts with him as proof, but no actions were taken. When the new county magistrate Wang Zonghan 汪宗翰(b. 1845) came to Dunhuang in April 1902, he was informed of the existence of Cave 17 and given several of its items. In turn, Wang Zonghan wrote about this to the epigrapher Ye Changshi 葉昌熾(1849–1917), who was Gansu provincial education commissioner from 1902 to 1906.13 Furthermore, it appears that Wang Yuanlu also showed a case of manuscripts to the Qing official Ting Dong 廷棟(1866–1918), but the latter did not regard these as important.14 Based on Stein’s expedition report, ‘news of the discovery having reached distant Lanzhou, specimens of the manuscripts were asked for from provincial headquarters’.15
zh: 或许期望因自己的虔诚之举获得某种经济补偿或认可，王圆箓立即将这一发现上报给了当地县令严泽（生卒年不详），并带去了两部写本作为证据，但却并未因此采取任何行动。1902年4月，新任县令汪宗翰（生于1845年）来到敦煌后，才得知第17窟的存在，并获赠了该窟的几件藏品。汪宗翰随后将此事写信告知了1902年至1906年间担任甘肃省教育专员的金石学家叶昌炽（1849–1917）。此外，王圆箓似乎还向清廷官员廷栋（1866–1918）展示过一些写本，但后者并未认为它们具有重要价值。根据斯坦因的考察报告，“这一发现的消息传到了遥远的兰州，省府便要求提供这些写本的样本”。

en: Wang Yuanlu was continuing or joining efforts to rehabilitate the site that had started before his arrival.30 As explained by the Russian army officer Vsevolod Ivanovich Roborovsky, limited repairs were already underway when he visited the Mogao Caves in 1894:
zh: 王圆箓在继续此前就已启动的对该遗址的修复工作，或是加入了这些修复行动。据俄罗斯军官弗谢沃洛德·伊万诺维奇·罗博罗夫斯基的描述，他在1894年造访莫高窟时，就已经有有限的修复工作在进行之中：

en: China today.40 Scholars have stressed that this particular branch of Daoism includes many elements that are indistinguishable from those of Buddhism.41 According to Rong Xinjiang, the aim of Wang’s restorations was to convert Buddhist halls into Daoist shrines.42 While Stein’s accounts referred to Wang’s works as ‘tokens of lingering Buddhist worship, genuine though distorted’,43 his travel diary did mention an ‘invasion of Taoist imagery’ in the shrines.44 Wang’s epitaph, inscribed on the tomb stone erected by two of his disciples in 1931, states that he was put in charge of the county’s Daoist Association by the magistrate Lu Qian 陸前in recognition of his merits. Importantly, the epitaph stresses Wang’s genuine dedication to restoring the Mogao Caves, including the Buddhist statues, as well as his endeavour to convince people to contribute money towards these efforts.45 As attested by a letter on red paper signed in his name, it seems that Wang Yuanlu even sent a plea for a large donation to the local administration following the transfer of Cave 17’s remaining contents to Beijing.46
zh: 《今日中国》40。有学者指出，这一派的道教包含许多与佛教毫无区别的要素。41据荣新江的研究，王圆箓进行修复工作的目的，是将佛教殿堂改造成道教祠堂。42虽然斯坦因将其所见的王圆箓的遗迹描述为“虽已扭曲但仍属于真实的佛教崇拜遗存”，43但他的游记中确实提到了这些祠堂里“充斥着道教意象”。441931年，王圆箓的两位弟子为他立碑刻写墓志，其中称他是因功绩突出而由陆前县令任命为该县道教协会负责人。重要的是，墓志强调了王圆箓对修复莫高窟——包括其中的佛教造像——的真诚奉献，以及他为争取人们捐资支持这些工作所付出的努力。45有一封以他名义签署的红色信件为证，在第17窟的剩余文物被运往北京之后，王圆箓似乎还向当地政府请求提供大额捐赠。46

en: It is therefore clear that being a Daoist did not preclude Wang from revering the Mogao Caves as a Buddhist site and devoting his existence to their upkeep. According to the stele ‘Record of the Thousand Buddha Caves’ Thousand Images Pagoda’ by Ting Dong, Wang Yuanlu collected several damaged Buddha statues in 1910 and placed them in a specially built pagoda.47 The pagoda was demolished in the 1940s and the artefacts it contained are now in the collections of the Dunhuang Academy.48 There is further evidence that Wang Yuanlu’s worship extended to the contents of Cave 17, particularly textual materials. We know of two instances in which he directly used the manuscripts from the cave for devotional and merit-making purposes. A document in the Dunhuang county archives dated to 1910 recorded that, in 1908, he ‘loaded some Buddhist scrolls into two barrel-like containers, tightly sealed these and placed them on wooden poles inside a Buddhist hall, calling them sūtra-turning wheels’.49 In 1944, the Dunhuang Academy also found 72 manuscripts inside a statue located in a Daoist temple built by Wang Yuanlu in the early 1900s.50 Given
zh: 由此可见，作为道教徒并不妨碍王圆箓将莫高窟视为佛教圣地，并毕生致力于其保护工作。根据丁东所著的《千佛洞记·千像塔》一文记载，王圆箓在1910年收集了几尊受损的佛像，并将它们安置在一座专门建造的塔中。47该塔在20世纪40年代被拆除，其中的文物如今藏于敦煌研究院。48还有更多证据表明，王圆箓的崇拜对象还包括第17窟内的各类物品，尤其是文献资料。目前可知有两次他直接利用该窟中的写本来用于修行积德之事：敦煌县档案馆中一份日期为1910年的文件记载，1908年时他曾“将一些佛教卷子装入两个类似桶状的容器中，严密封好后再把它们放在佛堂内的木杆上，称之为转经筒”。491944年，敦煌研究院还在王圆箓在20世纪初建造的一座道观里的雕像内发现了72份写本。50鉴于此

en: At some point between 1900 and 1904, Wang completely emptied Cave 17 before he received the order to put the whole ‘collection’ back in it.61 During this process, he must have had the opportunity to form an overall idea of everything that had been deposited in the small room prior to its sealing-off. Because the scattering of the cave’s contents started very soon after its discovery, this makes Wang Yuanlu the only person who was ever close to knowing their full extent and original arrangement. Stein wrote that Wang was looking for ‘valuables’.62 This somehow conveyed the image of Wang Yuanlu as an individual driven by greed. It would be more accurate to say that he was searching for valuable items, which could be understood in terms of their significance as well as their monetary value. Wasn’t the British-Hungarian explorer himself drawn to the Caves of the Thousand Buddhas by the promise of Cave 17’s hidden ‘treasures’?63 Wang could have decanted the cave to get a better understanding of what was in there, perhaps even to reorder its contents into an arrangement that he deemed more adequate.
zh: 在1900年至1904年间的某个时候，王圆箓在接到将全部“藏品”重新放回第17窟的命令之前，已先将该窟内的物品全部清空。在这一过程中，他必定有机会了解这个封闭前的小空间里曾存放过的一切。由于该洞窟的物品在被发现后很快就开始散落，这使得王圆箓成为唯一几乎掌握其全部内容与原有布局的人。斯坦因写道，王圆箓当时正在寻找“贵重物品”。这种说法无形中将王圆箓塑造成一个被贪婪驱使的人，但实际上更准确的说法应是他在搜寻具有价值的事物，而这些价值既包括其重要性，也包括其经济价值。难道这位英匈探险家本人被吸引到千佛洞，不也正是出于对第17窟中隐藏“宝藏”的期待吗？王圆箓很可能是为了更清楚地了解窟内的物品，甚至可能为了按照自己认为更合理的顺序重新排列这些物品，才将窟内物品全部倒出的。

en: Wang Yuanlu certainly did play a vital role in the organisation of Cave 17’s contents when he rehoused them. Stein described what were two very distinct kinds of bundles in the cave: the ‘regular’ bundles, composed of uniform packets containing canonical Buddhist texts in Chinese and Tibetan that may have once belonged to monastic libraries; and the ‘miscellaneous’ or ‘mixed’ bundles, filled with fragmentary Chinese and Tibetan rolls, non- Chinese texts, paintings, textiles, and other ex-votos.64 Wang had sorted and structured these bundles according to their type and physical characteristics. At the bottom, he had put several ‘miscellaneous’ bundles to ‘what he thought appropriate use in turning the floor at the foot of the north wall and on either side of the clay platform into a foundation level with the latter’.65 In his diary, Stein recorded that some of these bundles, which contained pictures and waste paper, may even have been placed there to keep off the damp.66 He had then built on this base a ‘wall-like array’ of ‘regular’ manuscript bundles, above which lay
zh: 王圆箓在重新整理第17窟内的藏物时，确实发挥了至关重要的作用。斯坦因描述了该窟中存在的两种截然不同的卷束：一类是“常规”卷束，由装订整齐的包袋构成，内含可能曾属于寺院藏书的汉文和藏文佛教经典；另一类则是“杂项”或“混合”卷束，其中装有零碎的汉文和藏文卷、非汉文文本、绘画、纺织品以及其他供奉物。王圆箓根据这些卷束的类型与物理特征对它们进行了分类整理。他在北墙底部及泥质平台两侧的地面之上，按照自己的设想对这些“杂项”卷束进行了处理，将其改造成与平台平齐的基底。斯坦因在日记中记载，其中一些装有图片和废纸的卷束，或许是被放置在那里用以防潮的。随后，他在这一基础上构建了一排类似墙状的“常规”写本卷束，其上方还摆放着其他物品。

en: The explorer remarked that ‘it was mere chance, too, what bundles the Tao-shih [Daoshi] would hand [them] out’.93 In fact, Wang was carefully planning what to deliver, focusing on the items he valued the least. The position of the ‘miscellaneous’ bundles made them easy to reach, but, more importantly, their selection was deliberate. While Wang Yuanlu appeared indifferent to Stein sifting through these bundles, he was by contrast eager to shield the regular ones from him: ‘The secret hope of diverting by their sacrifice my attention from the precious rolls of Chinese canonical texts or “Ching” [jing 經] made him now more assiduously grope for and hand out bundles of what he evidently classed under the head of miscellaneous rubbish.’94
zh: 这位探险家指出，“道士会把哪些卷束交给他们，这也纯属偶然”。实际上，王圆箓是在精心规划要交付哪些物品，他选择的是那些他自己认为价值最低的物件。那些“杂项”卷束的位置便于取用，但更重要的是，它们的挑选是经过刻意安排的。虽然王圆箓对斯坦因翻看这些卷束似乎毫不在意，但他却极力想保护那些“常规”的卷束不让他看到：“他暗自希望通过牺牲这些物品，将我的注意力从那些珍贵的中国经典文献卷轴，也就是‘经’上转移开，正因如此，他才更加卖力地搜寻并递出那些被他明确归类为杂项垃圾的卷束。”

en: Thanks to Jiang’s persuasion, Wang consented to letting them remove the items that they were putting aside, provided that they exercised the utmost discretion and acted in secret:95
zh: 在蒋孝琬的劝说下，王圆箓同意让他们拿走那些被他们搁置起来的物品，条件是他们必须极为谨慎行事，并秘密进行。

en: Wang Yuanlu did not want to be seen outside his quarters at night, so Jiang Xiaowan acted as courier, carrying documents back to Stein’s tent while everyone else slept.97 This demonstrates that Wang remained in control and dictated the terms of the transaction.
zh: 王圆箓不想在夜间出现在自己的住处外面，因此由蒋孝琬充当信使，在其他人都在睡觉时将文件送回斯坦因的帐篷。这表明王圆箓依然掌控着局面，并能决定交易的条款。

en: This passage demonstrates again that Wang was guiding the selection process and suggests that the local Buddhist community influenced negotiations, as Wang prioritised the monks’ interests in this instance. Although Wang Yuanlu ceded a large share of Chinese and Tibetan manuscripts, he controlled the transaction at every stage. Jiang Xiaowan’s rejection of several ‘lan-di’ (spoiled or decayed) bundles also indicates that Wang Yuanlu tried to release manuscripts of lesser value.125 By contrast, when selecting gifts for officials, Wang had chosen particularly fine manuscripts, with beautiful handwriting and in excellent condition. Upon leaving Dunhuang in mid June 1907, Stein had taken with him over 90 bundles of manuscripts, containing about 1,200 separate texts in rolls or ‘Pothis’. This new tranche of materials was even more significant: it comprised 230 of the regular bundles, ‘rais[ing] the number of texts to close on 4,000’.126
zh: 这段文字再次表明，王圆箓在指导挑选过程，并且暗示当地的佛教团体影响了谈判结果，因为在这一场合王圆箓优先考虑了僧侣们的利益。尽管王圆箓让出了大量中文和藏文写本，但他仍在每个阶段掌控着交易。蒋孝琬拒绝了若干“劣质”（已损坏或腐朽的）卷束，这也说明王圆箓试图处理那些价值较低的手稿。125 相比之下，在为官员挑选礼物时，王圆箓则选择了书写精美、状况极佳的优质写本。1907年6月中旬离开敦煌时，斯坦因带走了90多卷束写本，其中包含约1200份以卷或“Pothis”形式存在的独立文献。这批新获得的资料更为重要：它包含了230个常规卷束，“使得文献总数接近4000份”。126

en: had heard of the newly found repository at the Mogao Caves complex and had been shown an eighth-century manuscript from Cave 17.127 This had made him even more eager to reach the Thousand Buddha Caves, which were already on his itinerary when he left France. Once there, Pelliot also purchased a sizeable portion of the cave’s contents from Wang Yuanlu. Stein may have been the first Western explorer to see the newly discovered cache, but I would argue that Pelliot’s luck was to have come in second place. It may have resulted in his securing some of the ‘rarest’ pieces.
zh: 他曾听说过莫高窟群中新发现的藏经处，还有人向他展示过来自第17窟的八世纪写本。这让他更加渴望前往千佛洞，而该地本来就在他离开法国时的行程之中。抵达后，伯希和也从王圆箓手中购入了大量洞内藏品。尽管斯坦因可能是首位见到这些新发现藏品的西方探险家，但我认为伯希和能居次位实属幸运，这或许使他得以获得一些最为“稀有”的文物。
